cards.q: What is PIM-DM and how does it distribute multicast traffic?
cards.a: PIM-DM (Dense Mode) assumes almost every LAN has a receiver. It floods multicast into the network (a push model) and then prunes branches with no members, building trees directly from the source.
The source sends, traffic floods to all PIM neighbors, leaf routers without members send prunes, and after the prune state times out the network re-floods, which happens about every 3 minutes.

cards.q: What kind of tree does PIM-DM build?
cards.a: It builds a source-based shortest-path tree (SPT) rooted at the source, held as (S,G) state.

cards.q: Which multicast state entries does PIM-DM use?
cards.a: Only (S,G) per-source entries; wildcard (*,G) any-source entries are not used in dense mode.

cards.q: What is a graft in PIM-DM?
cards.a: A graft is the fast re-join message that restores a pruned branch when a new member appears below the prune point.

cards.q: How do you enable PIM-DM on a router?
cards.a: Enable multicast globally with ip multicast-routing, then configure ip pim dense-mode per interface.

cards.q: Does PIM-DM require a rendezvous point?
cards.a: No. PIM-DM is RP-less, so no RP configuration is needed.

cards.q: How does dense mode compare with sparse mode?
cards.a: Dense assumes members everywhere and pushes/floods with only (S,G) state and no RP; sparse assumes few members and pulls/joins using (*,G) then (S,G) with a required RP. Sparse is more efficient and is the production default.

cards.q: When is PIM-DM acceptable to use?
cards.a: For small, fully-meshed groups with dense receivers, such as LAN audio.
show ip mroute, show ip pim interface, and show ip pim neighbor; debug ip pim helps diagnose problems.

cards.q: A PIM-DM tree is not forming; what should you check?
cards.a: Whether ip pim dense-mode is enabled on the interfaces; use show ip mroute and show ip pim neighbor.

cards.q: What do graft storms indicate in a PIM-DM network?
cards.a: A flapping member that triggers repeated graft/prune cycles; fix the member's stability.

cards.q: What is the core exam distinction between the PIM-DM and PIM-SM trees?
cards.a: PIM-DM builds a source-based (S,G) SPT from the start with no RP; PIM-SM starts on a shared (*,G) tree through an RP before switching to the (S,G) SPT.
A push/flood model that uses only (S,G) state, needs no RP, builds an SPT from the source, auto-prunes empty branches, restores them with grafts, and is not the default; it suits dense LANs.
